name: Bone Meridian
description: A single canyon system runs from pole to pole along Bone Meridian's prime longitude, so deep and sheer that sunlight only reaches its floor for two hours each day. The canyon walls are striped in bands of white and grey stone that resemble exposed bone, giving the planet its name. On either side of this great divide, rolling highlands support forests of dark conifers dusted with perpetual frost.

The chill is constant and penetrating, even in the warmer months. Sound carries strangely across the canyon, conversations echoing for minutes after they end. In the forests, snow falls softly through needled branches, and the air smells of pine resin and cold stone. The planet feels ancient and patient, as though it has been waiting.

A repeating signal emanates from somewhere deep within the canyon, detected only at certain frequencies and only during the brief window when sunlight reaches the floor. Decades of study have produced no explanation for the signal's origin or meaning. The canyon walls show no caves or passages large enough to house transmitting equipment at the apparent source depth.

Bone Meridian's timber and silicate resources make it attractive to colonial interests, but the signal has drawn a steady stream of researchers and fringe theorists who oppose commercial development. Tensions between the scientific community and corporate surveyors have escalated to the point of minor sabotage. Whatever lies at the bottom of the meridian canyon may reshape understanding of the region's history, if anyone can reach it.
